sources.author: user
sources.annotation: aesthetics wise and use of colours, this is my favourite landing page. its very modern, i love the white background, uses tons of real world pictures. Their copy is also very strong using wording like 'This is what school should look like.' I want to do something very similar where we can say 'This is what learning should be like.' the use of storytelling in this landing page is great. I want something similiar where every section is connected and at the end we leave with a bold claim saying instead of everything going online its important to keep learning physical like no tech so that kids use their tablets less, learning is also shown to be scientifically superior when u write on paper, and also learning is different for every kid we make it personalized based on their progress difficulities etc.
sources.observe: Sirca display serif (400, Title Case, headlines end with a period) + Soehne body; white #FFFFFF; black 1px hairline grid framing every section; primary colour tiles yellow rgb(254,217,51), blue rgb(55,126,240), orange rgb(254,109,46), green rgb(0,173,111); hero = lineup of cut-out real kids; numbered cards 01-04; closing line '100% Real Primer Students. 0% Models. This Is What School Should Look Like.'
take: primary colour tiles as structure, not decoration
serif display headlines in Title Case
avoid: '0% models' style claim (we have no students yet)
copying Primer's exact hex values or fonts (commercial)

sources.author: user
sources.annotation: [hero] this is the best homepage i've seen in this space so far, its a delight and amazing experience of simply scrolling and using their landing page. I love the micro animations | [What's Included] what's included is a great section that we should also have to show the different aspects we offer like workbooks recieved by mall personalized every week based on the students progress, also other things like parent progress reports that update in realtime etc. | [Unlock / transformational] this is a strong use of hitting on the emotional side of the product the 'Unlock the full potential of every child and learning is transformational when the teaching responds'
sources.observe: Wallop rounded sans 600; deep teal ink; near-white blue-tinted background; tilted white-bordered word chips that swap with a spring (reading/math); looping product webm videos; 2 Rive mascot canvases; scattered real photos and handwritten notes drifting around a centred emotional line; hero line repeated as the closing CTA (bookend); 'What's Included' 6-card grid
take: micro animations: swapping word chip, drifting photos, card lift
emotional section with real photos and handwritten pages
bookend the hero line at the end
avoid: mascots and illustrated hills (kid-brand look; conflicts with Primer)
review counts, '88%' outcome stats, press logos (we have none)

sources.author: user
sources.annotation: [hero] i like how this hero section has an emotional appeal to it and leads with a bold claim 'The Future of Learning is Here'. Also this doesnt seem like ai slop they showcase a real student learning. However, this is a somewhat risky hero section, because anyone visiting should be able to quickly within 15 seconds understand what squirrel does, but the section after the hero is exactly that 'What is Squirrel AI' so i like that | [platform] we can do something similar where we go here -> what is our company / product, leading with the why us type of narrative -> and then we can go into our platform / our product and walk them through the user flow: Assess -> Deliver -> Practice -> Scan -> Adapt -> Repeat (6 steps as written)
take: emotional hero + bold claim + real child
'What is [Brand]?' section directly after the hero
narrative order: what/why us -> product -> user flow
avoid: stats band, press logos, centre franchise content

sources.author: user
sources.annotation: [hero] i like the hero section's use of real humans and how everything connects | [Why choose] we should do something like 'Why choose us?' we dont need to name our competitors / alternatives like the in person centres or online ai platforms, we simply need to show how we are a superior product doing something very unique and never been done before
sources.observe: hero = rounded photo pills of real kids joined by a dashed yellow line with yellow label chips; 'Why choose Outschool?' = 3 icon cards on a saturated purple band
take: real-people photos joined by a connecting line with label chips
'Why choose us?' cards without naming alternatives
